text:
maria: quick heads-up — saw a regressing tail-latency signal on paged-attn after last allocator tweak. 99.9th jumped ~2.3x on our long-context benchmark :grimacing:

aseem: ugh. which tweak? the slab hotpath change?

maria: yes, the hybrid-slab fallback that moves >64KB segments into pagehouse. repro profile attached (flamegraph + traces). perf-bot: perf alert (3523456790) — 99.9th latency 2.3x vs baseline.

kevin: can you paste the exact alloc flags you used for the run?

maria: here — run command:

```
./bench --model=gptx-large --seq=8192 --batch=4 --kv-mode=paged --alloc=hybrid-slab --slab-threshold=65536 --prefault=false --kernel-policy=auto
```

maria: notable: prefault=false, slab-threshold=64k, kernel-policy=auto (allow flashv2->fallback).

jess: what's the observable behavior? higher CPU? more io?

maria: interesting pattern: during hot churn windows we see many small slab splits and immediate promotions into pagehouse. KV lookup time per token increases (miss penalty) and kernel chooser backs off to fallback kernel more often. trace snippet: "kv_page_migrate" spikes aligned with tail events.

aseem: screenshot of allocator counters?

maria: counters (samples):
- slab_allocs: 1.2M
- slab_splits: 18k
- page_promote_ops: 42k
- kv_page_faults: 9.1k
- pagehouse_inflight_io_ms: p95=42ms p99=128ms

maria: and kernel-choice transitions: flashv2->flashv1 fallback_rate p95=12% (baseline 1.1%)

kevin: that fallback_rate is the smoking gun. fallback kernel has worse throughput and higher per-token overhead. But why are we promoting to pagehouse so aggressively?

jess: maybe the slab threshold interacts badly with sequential token churn. If tokens keep growing beyond 64k chunk, allocator splits and the policy triggers promote-to-pagehouse on split. Could be a policy bug.

maria: I instrumented allocation path; note this sequence: allocate slab chunk -> write KV -> next step writes more keys that fall into adjacent range -> allocator split -> promote one split half to pagehouse because remote_free_estimator thinks fragmentation >0.7 -> pagehouse copy -> afterwards access hits KV page fault then IO.

aseem: remote_free_estimator threshold 0.7 seems too aggressive for long seq workloads. Might be tuned for small-chat workloads.

kevin: can you repro with prefault=true (force physical backing on alloc) to see if IO disappears? Also try raising slab-threshold to 256k so fewer splits.

maria: ran both quickly: prefault=true reduces page_promote_ops by ~80% and p99 latency back to near baseline. slab-threshold=256k also reduces splits but increases memory pressure slightly.

perf-bot: quick perf snapshot (3523456950):
- baseline p99: 18ms
- current p99: 42ms
- with prefault p99: 20ms

jess: that indicates the promote path is causing IO amplification. If kernel chooser sees more page faults it flips to fallback kernels because they have more conservative memory access patterns. Our fallback kernel selection logic includes a composite metric: (page_fault_rate * alpha) + (seq_len_variance * beta). Maybe alpha is too high.

aseem: two actionable items then: 1) short-term: increase remote_free_estimator threshold and enable prefault for long-seq profiles 2) medium-term: adjust kernel-policy to be less sensitive to transient page faults and prefer micro-batching fallback only after sustained faults.

kevin: also add a fast-path: if split->promote happens within a 10ms window of the alloc and promote IO is > X ms, don't change kernel policy until window elapses. Prevent thrash.

maria: I'll put up a minimal patch: remote_free_estimator default -> 0.85 for workloads with avg_seq > 4k; add config flag "kernel_policy.cooldown_ms=50". will run nightly bench.

jess: add a telemetry span for "promote_latency_ms" (histogram) so we can feed it into kernel chooser instead of raw fault rate.

maria: noted. repro steps and diff:
1) run bench with sequence churn profile attached (attached JSON)
2) reproduce 2x tail by using hybrid-slab + slab-threshold=64k + prefault=false
3) apply patch branch: github.com/redwood-inference/allocors/pull/487

kevin: good. also add an e2e smoke that runs kernel-policy=auto on long-context model for 10 minutes to catch regressions in CI.

maria: will do. planning: ship prefault toggle to canary today, change estimator next week, kernel cooldown after validation.

perf-bot: note created: todo (3523457001) — canary rollout prefault toggle to dedicated pools.

aseem: thanks, everyone. feel free to DM if you need extra IO capacity for repro. :thumbsup:
